Trying to fix that because it's a horrendous correctness bug on basic, fixed-size matmuls that affects both CPU and GPU backends. And the current workaround in e2e matmul tests is annoying to carry around.

Trying to drop the work-around today, causes 27 e2e matmul tests to fail out of 85 running here (CPU + ROCm).  Failing tests are CPU tests, and ROCm tests with VectorDistribution.  The first failing CPU test is a simple vecmat, static shape:

```mlir
util.func @matmul_accumulate_1x1000xi8_times_1000x1000xi8_into_1x1000xi32(%lhs: tensor<1x1000xi8>, %rhs: tensor<1000x1000xi8>, %acc: tensor<1x1000xi32>) -> tensor<1x1000xi32> {
  %result = linalg.matmul   ins(%lhs, %rhs: tensor<1x1000xi8>, tensor<1000x1000xi8>) outs(%acc: tensor<1x1000xi32>) -> tensor<1x1000xi32>
  util.return %result: tensor<1x1000xi32>
}
```

The first failing GPU test, ROCm+VectorDistribution, is a static-shape ` (MxKxN): 512x128x512`

Reproduction is as simple as (failing vecmat shape on CPU):

Since you're suspecting MaterializeCOW, here is the IR dump before/after it:
https://gist.github.com/bjacob/0c04d8e3f5346bd16f194a839416c264
@benvanik , can you see something in that IR dump ?

This is specific to static shapes - dynamic shapes work fine.

On CPU with generic x86 target (so using only SSE2 or some such) for `i8` matmuls,
* Shape 1x64x75  (MxKxN) succeeds
* Shape 1x64x76  (MxKxN) fails.

Test files and print-ir-after-all logs in this archive:

[logs.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22601595/logs.zip)

Reproduction:
```
➜  iree-build tools/iree-compile ~/64x75.mlir --iree-hal-target-backends=llvm-cpu --iree-opt-data-tiling --iree-llvmcpu-enable-ukernels=none --iree-llvmcpu-target-cpu=generic -o ~/a.vmfb -mlir-disable-threading -mlir-print-ir-after-all 2>~/log-64x75.mlir
➜  iree-build tools/iree-compile ~/64x76.mlir --iree-hal-target-backends=llvm-cpu --iree-opt-data-tiling --iree-llvmcpu-enable-ukernels=none --iree-llvmcpu-target-cpu=generic -o ~/a.vmfb -mlir-disable-threading -mlir-print-ir-after-all 2>~/log-64x76.mlir
```

The IR shows that it fails whenever the sizes are aligned to a multiple of the DT tile size, as then there is no pack/unpack of the accumulator and it can return the raw accumulator, exposing the aliasing bug.

Shape 1x8x8 fails already.
Taking a look again. This was a hairy issue x_x

Hi! I have stumbled upon a related bug that appears in very simple programs.
The problem is that input buffers are overwritten that shouldn't be overwritten.
(I am exploring the use of IREE in an accelerated array computing framework for R I am working on (https://github.com/r-xla/anvl) and I am running my test suite against the IREE compiler and am tracking down the test failures).

Below is a simple program where the input is overwritten although it shouldn't be:

```mlir
func.func @main(%lhs: tensor<2x2xf32>, %rhs: tensor<2x2xf32>, %acc: tensor<2x2xf32>)
    -> (tensor<2x2xf32>, tensor<2x2xf32>) {
  %r = linalg.matmul ins(%lhs, %rhs : tensor<2x2xf32>, tensor<2x2xf32>)
                     outs(%acc : tensor<2x2xf32>) -> tensor<2x2xf32>
  return %r, %acc : tensor<2x2xf32>, tensor<2x2xf32>
}
```

```
--input=2x2xf32=1,2,3,4 --input=2x2xf32=1,0,0,1 --input=2x2xf32=100,100,100,100

result[0]: [101 102][103 104]
result[1]: [101 102][103 104]      <-- %acc, returned unchanged; should be 100s
```


Below is Claude's analysis:

---


The `TODO(#16168)` workarounds are also still live at HEAD — 5 occurrences
across `tests/e2e/matmul/generate_code.py`, `generate_code_mx.py` and
`tests/e2e/convolution/generate_e2e_conv2d_tests.py`.

**Why #22844 doesn't reach it.** That PR guards an existing clone during
elision, but in this shape no clone is ever created, so there is nothing for
the guard to see. `MaterializeCopyOnWrite.cpp`'s `isSafeToElideCOW()` rejects
block args, `Constant` lifetime and multi-user values, then returns `true` —
it never consults `TensorImportOp::getConsume()` or the `External` lifetime.
A borrowed import with a single user takes that path.

Pass-level reproducer, same pipeline as `elide_materialized_copies.mlir`:

```mlir
util.func public @borrowed_import_mutated(%view: !util.buffer) -> !util.buffer {
  %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
  %c64 = arith.constant 64 : index
  %c123_i32 = arith.constant 123 : i32
  %size = stream.tensor.sizeof tensor<256xf32> : index
  %buffer = stream.tensor.import %view : !util.buffer -> tensor<256xf32>
              in !stream.resource<external>{%size}
  %fill = stream.async.fill %c123_i32, %buffer[%c0 to %c64 for %c64]
            : i32 -> %buffer as !stream.resource<external>{%size}
  %out = stream.tensor.export %fill : tensor<256xf32>
           in !stream.resource<external>{%size} -> !util.buffer
  util.return %out : !util.buffer
}
```

```console
$ iree-opt --pass-pipeline='builtin.module(util.func(iree-stream-materialize-copy-on-write),iree-stream-elide-async-copies,cse,canonicalize)' borrow.mlir
```

Output is unchanged — no clone inserted. Adding `consume` changes only the
keyword. If the clone is written in by hand, #22844's `containsBorrowedStorage`
walk does preserve it, so the fix works; nothing reaches it. This is the dual
of the file's existing `@inplace_fill_imported_buffer`, which #22844 edited to
add `consume`.

**Two flag notes**, since they decide whether you see it:

- Default `--iree-execution-model=async-internal` fails as above. Under
  `async-external` the two-result form is correct on 3.12 (that half does look
  fixed) — but a *single-use* import still gets `rw` on the borrowed resource
  and `util.return %arg0`, which is the ordinary sort/top-k shape and what a
  PJRT client meets, since `integrations/pjrt` sets `async-external`.
- `iree.abi.consume` on the argument has no effect either way: it reaches
  `stream.tensor.import consume` and the generated code is byte-identical.

**Versions.** Reproduced on stock wheels `3.11.0rc20260316` and
`3.12.0rc20260831`, Linux x86_64, `--iree-hal-target-device=local`,
`llvm-cpu`. No commit since 2026-08-31 touches `MaterializeCopyOnWrite.cpp`,
`ElideAsyncCopies.cpp` or `test/materialize_copy_on_write.mlir`; that pass has
had no behavioural change since 710287135c (2024-05-28).

Possibly related: #13003, open since 2023, reports the same pass ignoring
operand/result tying at `util.call` boundaries.

We hit this through `integrations/pjrt` from a non-JAX client, where a top-k
call leaves the caller's input array holding the sorted values. Happy to open a
separate issue for that side if you'd rather keep this one scoped to the
compiler.

Here is another example that fails:

```mlir
func.func @main(%a: tensor<6xf32>) -> tensor<6xf32> {
  %r = "stablehlo.sort"(%a) ({
  ^bb0(%x: tensor<f32>, %y: tensor<f32>):
    %c = stablehlo.compare GT, %x, %y : (tensor<f32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<i1>
    stablehlo.return %c : tensor<i1>
  }) {dimension = 0 : i64, is_stable = true} : (tensor<6xf32>) -> tensor<6xf32>
  return %r : tensor<6xf32>
}
```

Then run:

```python
host = np.array([1, 5, 2, 6, 3, 4], dtype=np.float32)
dev  = rt.asdevicearray(cfg.device, host)
out  = ctx.modules.module["main"](dev)
```

```
input before : [1. 5. 2. 6. 3. 4.]
result       : [6. 5. 4. 3. 2. 1.]
input after  : [6. 5. 4. 3. 2. 1.]     <-- the caller's own buffer
```
